hook.line: Five Claude commands almost nobody uses, and they change the model.
hook.visual: Bearded man holding a mic in an office; yellow/white title '5 Claude commands cut tokens by 75%' on top; he holds up five fingers as captions start.

beats.what: Title card promises 5 commands and a 75% token cut; five fingers raised.
Problem framing: people run Claude on default and it sounds generic.
Setup: the switches already exist, they just look like terminal commands.
Command 1, /caveman: strips around 75% of response tokens.
Command 2, ultrathink, shown as a dark UI pill sticker at the top.
Command 3, /ghost, pill sticker 'strips AI tells'; lists no preamble, no em dashes.
Command 4, deepthink: slower but higher quality on complex questions.
Bonus: drop a side request into a running job without breaking it.
Close-up after a cut: payoff restated, 75% of token bill gone with /caveman.

why_it_works: Number and result in the title from frame one (5 commands, 75% fewer tokens), so the viewer knows the payoff and counts along.
Five fingers held up while saying 'five' turns the list promise into a physical gesture in the first second.
Each command gets a small UI-style pill at the top, giving a scannable visual anchor that looks like the real product.
Ends by repeating the biggest number, which loops back to the title (loop 0.855).
weaknesses: One static shot for 35.6 s; only 2 cuts, so energy rests entirely on the speaker.
Promises five commands but only some get a pill graphic; the list is hard to track without a counter.
Captions sit over the chest in the middle band, mostly outside the safe area (0.932 share).
No explicit CTA at the end.
for_robert: Pop a small product-UI pill (the command name) near the top each time a list item starts; Fred could carry or point at that pill instead of it appearing flat, and hold up fins as a counter.
